label.en: ⚠️ Cambridge 9709 Traps — Exam Pacing & Standard Accuracy

body.en:
Pacing on Paper 3: With 75 marks in 1 hour 50 minutes (110 minutes), you have roughly 1.45 minutes per mark. High-mark synoptic questions (differential equations, complex numbers with geometry, 3D vectors) typically appear toward the back of the paper and demand 15–20 minutes of sustained focus.

Cambridge Standard Accuracy Rule: Unless a question specifies otherwise, non-exact numerical values must be given correct to 3 significant figures, and angles in degrees to 1 decimal place. Premature rounding during intermediate steps is a frequent cause of losing the final A1 mark. Always store exact surd/fraction values or at least 4 significant figures in calculator memory registers.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (About A2 Level)

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

label.en: Worked Example A — About A2 Level (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): The box plot for dataset \( U \) has quartiles \( Q_1 = 11 \), median \( M = 21 \), and \( Q_3 = 28 \). Find the interquartile range \( v = Q_3 - Q_1 \) of \( U \).

Step-by-Step Solution: The interquartile range is \( Q_3 - Q_1 = 28 - 11 = 17 \).

label.en: Worked Example B — About A2 Level (Medium Application)

body.en:
Problem (Medium): Given \( X\sim U(-1,14) \), find \( \text{Var}(X) \).

Step-by-Step Solution: \( \text{Var}(X)=\dfrac{(b-a)^2}{12}=\dfrac{15^2}{12}=\dfrac{225}{12}=\dfrac{75}{4} \). Final Answer: \(\dfrac{75}{4}\).

label.en: Worked Example C — About A2 Level (Hard Application)

body.en:
Problem (Hard): For finite sets \( H \) and \( J \), \( |H| = 60 \), \( |J| = 54 \), and \( |H \cap J| = 24 \). Find the union cardinality \( v = |H \cup J| \).

Step-by-Step Solution: By Inclusion-Exclusion, \( |H \cup J| = 60 + 54 - 24 = 90 \).

label.en: Worked Example D — About A2 Level (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): A normal random variable \( U \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu = 94, \sigma^2 = 25) \) is observed at \( v = 104 \). Find the standardized score \( z = (v - \mu)/\sigma \).

Step-by-Step Solution: The \( z \)-score is \( \frac{104 - 94}{5} = 2 \).

rows.en: The \(25\%\) reduction applies to the larger base \(1.25 Q_0\), not \(Q_0\).
Dividing by a negative number reverses order on the real number line.
Flip the inequality symbol whenever multiplying or dividing by a negative: \(x < -4\).
Computing round-trip average speed as \(\frac{v_1 + v_2}{2}\)
Time spent at the slower speed is longer than time spent at the faster speed.
Use total distance over total time: \(v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

label.en: ▲ Exam Pacing & Verification Strategy — About A2 Level

body.en: High-Speed Exam Shortcut (Cambridge International A Level (9709 Paper 3 / Paper 6)): When a linear system asks for a combined expression like \(3x + 3y\) rather than \(x\) and \(y\) individually, add or subtract the two equations directly before isolating either variable—this often yields the target expression in a single step.

question.en: A student calculates \(\int_1^3 \frac{4}{2x+1}\,dx\) by rounding \(\ln 7 \approx 1.95\) and \(\ln 3 \approx 1.10\) at the start, obtaining \(2(1.95 - 1.10) = 1.70\). State the exact value of the integral and calculate the absolute error introduced by premature rounding.

solution.en:
Integrate exactly:

\[\int_1^3 \frac{4}{2x+1}\,dx = [2\ln(2x+1)]_1^3 = 2\ln 7 - 2\ln 3 = 2\ln\left(\frac{7}{3}\right) \approx 1.6946\dots\]

The exact value is \(2\ln\left(\frac{7}{3}\right)\). The premature rounding gives \(1.70\), yielding an absolute error of:

\[|1.70 - 1.6946| \approx 0.0054\]

On Cambridge Paper 3, this premature rounding costs the final accuracy mark (A1) because the 3 s.f. answer is 1.69, not 1.70.

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in About A2 Level and start from \(\int_1^3 \frac{4}{2x+1}\,dx\).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Isolate the primary variable or parameter systematically and simplify like terms before substituting numerical values.
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

question.en: [Practice 2 · Medium] A cumulative frequency distribution \( U(v) \) has \( Q_1 = 18 \), median \( 30 \), and \( Q_3 = 40 \). Find the spread \( \text{IQR}(U) = Q_3 - Q_1 \).

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in About A2 Level and start from \( U(v) \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( Q_3 - Q_1 = 40 - 18 = 22 \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

solution.en: From the cumulative frequency curve, \( Q_3 - Q_1 = 40 - 18 = 22 \).

question.en: [Practice 3 · Hard] In a two-stage probability tree for events \( H \) and \( J \), \( P(H) = 0.8 \) and \( P(J \mid H) = 0.6 \). Find the expected frequency \( v = 100 \cdot P(H \cap J) \) in \( 100 \) independent trials.

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in About A2 Level and start from \( H \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( P(H \cap J) = 0.8 \times 0.6 = 0.48 \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

solution.en: Since \( P(H \cap J) = 0.8 \times 0.6 = 0.48 \), the expected count in 100 trials is \( 48 \).
